subject: CascadePay - quant profile v2.3: latency surge & error-rate escalation
messages:
From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@cascadepay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 latency & error spike after this morning's quant deploy

Team — we pushed a high-volume inference job this morning and started seeing a p99 latency jump from ~320ms to 1.6s and a backend error-rate (5xx) increase to ~2.8% starting ~08:33 PDT (deploy at 08:30). This is across our checkout and fraud-check endpoints; throughput has dropped ~18%.

Attached are our sampling traces and the carrier logs (prod_trace_20260903.json.gz) showing repeated KV misses and occasional OOMs on a small subset of requests. We rolled some traffic to our fallback region which helped but can't sustain it. This is impacting live checkouts.

We need immediate remediation and an exec sync — our ops team is concerned about hitting contractual SLOs. Please advise rollback or mitigation steps.

Tom
Tom Evans
Head of Engineering, CascadePay
ops@cascadepay.com

Attachments: prod_trace_20260903.json.gz, tail_latency_screenshot.png

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-09-03T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency & error spike after this morning's quant deploy

Tom / Priya — initial engineering triage below. Note I copied this into the thread for visibility.

Observed (from traces + runtime telemetry):
- The quant profile v2.3 introduced a condensed weight layout and a different kernel selection path for the attention matmuls. That path increases register pressure for sequences >256 tokens and causes higher KV eviction rates in our runtime's LRU-based cache.
- Result: repeated KV cache-misses and extra recompute for hot keys -> sustained p99 increases. On some nodes the memory working set nudged above the configured limit triggering transient OOMs in a small fraction (~0.6%) of requests which surface as 5xx.

Immediate mitigations (recommended order):
1) Canary rollback to quant profile v2.2 for 20% of traffic — expect p99 to drop to baseline within a single rolling window (10–15 mins).
2) If canary looks good, revert all traffic to v2.2 (estimated 90–120 mins total to reach full traffic).
3) Short-term config patch: reduce dynamic batch max-size by 20% to reduce memory spikes during rollover (non-invasive).

I'll start the canary rollback if CascadePay approves. I'll also open INF-9052 and attach the traces. ETA for a canary is ~45m once we get go-ahead.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Staff SWE, Runtime & Serving, Redwood Inference
